rating.summary: The FOMC voted unanimously 12-0 to raise the federal funds rate by 25 basis points to a target range of 3-3/4 to 4 percent. The Committee cited solid economic activity, resilient domestic spending, strong productivity, and robust capital investment, while noting that inflation remains elevated. The statement reflects a continued tightening posture aimed at returning inflation to the 2 percent goal.
rating.stance_rationale: A 25bp rate hike with a unanimous vote and a firm commitment to deliver price stability signals a moderately hawkish stance, though the measured pace and absence of explicit forward guidance for further hikes tempers the hawkishness.
key_quotes: The Committee decided to raise the target range for the federal funds rate by 1/4 percentage point to 3-3/4 to 4 percent, in support of the Federal Reserve's dual mandate.
The Committee will deliver price stability.
